narrative.northStar: Luces apagadas: el café internet a las 9 de la noche
narrative.overview:
Nexos is the neighbourhood internet café after dark, open to any player. The room is a dim wall (pared) lined with purple cubicles; the only light comes from monitors, an amber "abierto" sign over the counter, and the green of a session timer or a live match. Every surface is a piece of that room: the top bar is the counter (mostrador), cards are cubicles, featured content is a poster taped to the wall, and signing in is "sitting down" in a cubicle.

Density is that of a working café, not a showroom: real data (prices per store, live matches, forum posts) is put on the wall in readable rows, numbers in a monospaced readout, headings on painted-sign letterforms. Light is scarce and meaningful: colour is spent on what is lit (a price, a live match, the open sign, the current choice), never on decoration.

The world rejects the dark eSports portal with purple-fuchsia neon and the grid of identical cards under a centred headline. No neon glow, no glass, no decorative gradients.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, warm-purple ground; light only where something is on, priced or live.
Cubicles (4px corners, 1px border) as the base container; taped, slightly rotated posters for featured content.
Painted-sign display type (Bricolage Grotesque 800), plain interface type (Onest), monospaced readouts for data only.
Motion as physical café behaviour: a sign tube flickering on, posters peeling off the wall, rolling price counters.
Everything collapses to short fades under prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The Lit-Things-Only Rule
rules.body: Colour other than the purples means something is lit. Amber = price, deal, the open sign, the active nav underline, focus. Green = live now. If it is not priced and not live, it is monitor white or purple.

rules.name: The Brand-Band Rule
rules.body: A game's own brand colour may appear only as the 4px top band of its poster (`--juego`), the way a printed poster has a colour strip. Never as a fill, text colour, or page theme.

rules.name: The No-Neon Rule
rules.body: No glows, no glass, no decorative gradients. Gradients are allowed only as dark scrims (pared at 0.3–0.97 alpha) under text laid over game art, and as the skeleton shimmer.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Mono is a readout, not a style: it sets prices, scores, times and counters, with tabular numerals. Words stay in Onest.

rules.name: The Sign Rule
rules.body: All h1–h4 use the letrero face at -0.02em to -0.03em tracking with balanced wrapping. Headings sit directly on the wall; nothing small and uppercase is stacked above them.

rules.name: The Off-The-Wall Rule
rules.body: Only posters and floating lists cast shadows. A cubicle never does; give it depth with tone and border.

dos: Do build every container as a cubicle: cubiculo fill, 1px cubiculo-2 border, 4px corners.
Do reserve amber for prices, deals, the "abierto" sign, the active nav underline and focus; reserve green for what is live and the session timer.
Do set every price, score, date, count and timer in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals.
Do put game brand colour only in a poster's 4px top band.
Do use a dark pared scrim (not a coloured gradient) whenever text sits over game art.
Do give featured content the poster treatment (rotation −1.2° to +1.4°, tape, poster shadow) and keep ordinary lists as flat cubicles.
Do provide a reduced-motion path for every animation.
donts: Don't use neon glows, glassmorphism or decorative gradients.
Don't place kickers or eyebrows (small uppercase labels) above headings.
Don't mark cards with coloured side stripes; identity bands go on the top edge only.
Don't use mono for words, labels or headings.
Don't spend amber or green on generic links, icons or decoration.
Don't add shadows to cubicles, buttons or fields.
Don't build a row of identical cards under a centred headline.
